bounded UTF-8 workspace reads and digest-bound workspace writes

evidence: Fresh local evidence: 71 default ordivon-exec tests, 95 default workspace tests, and 78 M1-feature ordivon-exec tests passed; strict workspace, M1-feature, and combined P2+M1 Clippy passed. A real root/systemd integration journey used 14 independent CLI processes to create and modify an isolated worktree, run an AI-authored Python tool, recover it after the initiating process exited, read three terminal Artifacts, detect untracked outputs, and cancel a second Task. The governed run completed in 2226 ms, denied /etc writes and systemd control, and left no residual units, processes, stores, or host escape file.
verification_result: M1 is verified as a feature-gated local universal-executor vertical slice. It proves durable cross-call execution and bounded Artifacts, but it does not prove Legacy performance superiority or production readiness.
degraded_reasons: The Task registry is filesystem-based and has no transactional idempotency or concurrency reservation.
The constrained runner still executes under root UID.
Filesystem read visibility is not yet a complete least-privilege view.
Task listing, retention, garbage collection, and full orphan reconciliation are absent.
Legacy Desktop Commander comparison is pending M2.
No MCP execution tool or production route is exposed.
Repository document governance retains three exact-base violations.
remaining_debt: Run M2 differential evaluation through Legacy and Ordivon using the same task journey.
Replace the filesystem Task registry with transactional admission and idempotency after performance evidence justifies it.
Introduce a dedicated non-root execution identity and narrower read visibility.
Add Task listing, retention, garbage collection, and stronger orphan recovery.
Define scoped network and credential opt-in without widening the default sandbox.
Do not expose production MCP execution or cut over Legacy traffic before comparative evidence and explicit authorization.
